decision.explanation: The derivative is y'=2/\sqrt{x}-4, so the tangent slope at x=1 is -2. Its equation is y=-2(x-1)=-2x+2. Setting x=0 gives the y-axis intersection (0,2).

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=4\sqrt{x}-4x$ at  $(1,0)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4\sqrt{x}-4x.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\sqrt{x}-4x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{1/2}-4x) \\  & =2{x}^{-1/2}-4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=2(1)^{-1/2}-4=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(0) & =-2(x-1) \\ y & =-2x+2-0 \\ y & =-2x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2(0)+2=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $(0,2).$

y=−2(0)+2=2.

decision.explanation: Differentiating y=4x^{-3}-x gives y'=-12x^{-4}-1. At x=1, the slope is -13. Using (1,3), the tangent is y-3=-13(x-1), which simplifies to y=-13x+16.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{3x+2}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3x+2}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3}{x}+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3}{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{-1})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{-2}) \\  & =-3{x}^{-2}-4{x}^{-3} \\  & =-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(-1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & =-\frac{3}{(-1)^{2}}-\frac{4}{(-1)^{3}} \\  & =-3+4 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=1$ and the coordinates of our point $(-1,-1),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-1) & =1\cdot (x-(-1)) \\ y+1 & =x+1 \\ y & =x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={f}^{′}(4) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2\sqrt{x}) \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}) \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{1/2}) \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={f}^{′}(4) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-4) & =-\frac{1}{2}(x-4) \\ y+4 & =-\frac{1}{2}x+2 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{2}x+2-4 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{2}x-2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{2}(0)-2 \\ y & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,-2).$
